paras: The attempted lynching near Pine Grove was the capture and threatened lynching of an unnamed man by a pursuing party in the woods near Pine Grove, apparently in Pennsylvania, reported in August 1881. The man, accused of attacking a young woman on Scalp's Mountain north of Port Clinton, was spared after he pleaded for mercy and was sent to jail. The only report found does not give his race.

According to the Lancaster Daily Intelligencer, Miss Mary Gerhardt, aged 18, was crossing Scalp's Mountain, five miles north of Port Clinton, when "a rough-looking man jumped out from the bush" and seized her. She struggled and freed herself after breaking her parasol over his head. News of the "attempted outrage" spread, and a party set out in pursuit and found the man in the woods near Pine Grove.

The party then made preparations to lynch him, but, in the paper's words, "his pleadings for mercy saved him, and he was sent to jail." The report names neither the man nor any member of the party, and it gives no date for the incident or the size of the group.
No report of a charge, trial or later disposition of the case was found in the coverage.

The episode survives in a single paragraph in the "State Items" column of the Lancaster Daily Intelligencer of 25 August 1881, printed between notes on a Clearfield fire truck and an indicted forger. The item treated the alleged attack as fact, called the accused "the villain" and "a rough-looking man", and reported the preparations to lynch him without comment. It used no racial terms, and no other paper's version of the story was found.
